query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A minor substitutional addition of Zr (around 2–3 atomic percent) into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy will improve its load‐bearing integrity and resistance to cracking while maintaining its large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with excellent caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.intervention: Substitute approximately 2–3 at% of the constituent elements (e.g., loosely replacing a minor portion of the transition metals) with zirconium (Zr).
generation.conditions: Operate over the same applied-field, pressure-field, and temperature regimes as the original alloy, with loading levels up to those at which cracking currently occurs.
generation.structural_mediator: Enhanced lattice distortion and potential formation of fine-scale precipitates or strengthened solid solution zones due to the large atomic size mismatch of Zr with the matrix elements.
generation.mechanism: The addition of Zr is expected to increase yield strength and improve toughness by causing stronger solid solution strengthening and controlled lattice distortions without significantly altering the phase responsible for the caloric (magneto- and baro-caloric) response. Keeping the Zr content low should avoid shifting or broadening the caloric phase transition.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the unchanged alloy, the Zr-doped alloy should show higher load-bearing integrity (improved yield stress and reduced crack initiation) while exhibiting a caloric response (entropy/temperature change under field or pressure) of similar magnitude.
generation.baseline: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with large caloric performance but poor mechanical properties (low toughness, high cracking tendency).
generation.boundary: The Zr addition is limited to around 2–3 at% to avoid excessive formation of secondary intermetallic compounds or altering the caloric phase transition significantly. Testing should remain within the operating field, pressure, temperature and load boundaries typical for solid refrigeration applications.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain how the minor Zr addition will quantitatively affect the caloric transition temperature and sharpness. The balance between mechanical improvement and potential dilution or shift of the caloric effect requires experimental verification.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the baseline (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy and another set with 2–3 at% Zr substituted into the matrix. Subject both sets to identical processing conditions. Perform standard mechanical tests (e.g., compression, bending, and fracture toughness tests) as well as caloric property measurements (e.g., adiabatic temperature change and entropy change under applied magnetic fields and hydrostatic pressure) over the relevant temperature and field ranges.
measurements: Crack initiation and propagation behavior under cyclic loading
Magnitude and sharpness of the caloric effect (e.g., ΔTad and ΔS)
Phase characterization (using XRD or TEM) to confirm preservation of key caloric phases
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Zr-doped alloy does not show a statistically significant improvement in mechanical integrity (e.g., yield strength and reduced cracking) compared to the baseline, or if the caloric performance (ΔTad or ΔS) is reduced or its transition significantly broadened/shifted, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Moreover, the addition of Zr can form an excessive atomic size difference (δ) with other elements and cause lattice distortion due to its large atomic radius, which can promote the formation of intermetallic compounds, resulting in the enhancement of mechanical properties []. Based on above, novel Wx(TaVZr)100−x RHEAs were designed and prepared. The effects of various W contents on their microstructural characteristics and compressive mechanical properties were systematically investigated. The underlying mechanisms for the phase formation and strengthening of the RHEAs were also examined and discussed.
